title: Maria and the eclipse
hook: Maria bears him a son, Ibrahim, who dies as a baby, and on the day of an eclipse he says the sun and moon don't eclipse for anyone's death (Bukhari)
carry: the eyes weep, the heart grieves

segments.voice: Yesterday, Safiyyah and Maymunah, and a taunt that didn't go unanswered. Your line was he defended her. Was there a moment you spoke up for someone, or wished you had? Day eight hundred seventeen.

The sky over Medina goes dim in broad daylight. The sun is being eaten from one side. On the ground, the town is already in mourning, because that same day a baby has died: Ibrahim, the son of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. People look up, then look at each other, and the talk begins. Of course the sun went dark. The heavens are grieving his son. It's a kind thing to say. It would comfort a father. Today: Maria, her son, and what he said under that dark sky.
screen: `THE SUN GOES DIM BY DAY.` → `A BABY HAS DIED THE SAME DAY.` → `THE HEAVENS ARE GRIEVING?`

segments.voice: Ibrahim's mother was Maria, remembered as Maria the Copt. Tradition, in Ibn Sa'd's biographies, says she came to Medina from Egypt, sent by its ruler. Some count her among the mothers of the believers; others give her a different standing, as the mother of his son. She's honored either way, and this is where our part on the mothers ends. Now the boy. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Anas tells of the day they went in to Ibrahim as he was dying. The Prophet's eyes filled with tears. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, surprised, asked: you too, messenger of God? And he answered: this is mercy. Then he said the line we carry today: the eyes weep, the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. And he spoke to the child: we are saddened by your parting, Ibrahim. Notice what that sentence allows. Tears, openly. Sorrow, named. And one limit: no words of protest against God. Then the eclipse. Another report in Bukhari, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, says the sun was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim died, and people said it was for his death. The Prophet answered them: the sun and the moon are two of the signs of God, and they are not eclipsed for anyone's death or life. When you see it, pray and call on God until it clears. He could have let the kind story stand. It was flattering, and it was about his own child. He corrected it on the day of his grief. That's why Muslims keep an eclipse prayer, salat al-kusuf: the dark sky becomes a time to pray, not a message about any one person. Grief that is real, and truth that isn't bent to comfort it.
screen: `MARIA, MOTHER OF IBRAHIM.` · `THIS IS MERCY.` · `NOT FOR ANYONE'S DEATH OR LIFE.` · `THE ECLIPSE BECOMES A TIME TO PRAY.` · then, large: `THE EYES WEEP, THE HEART GRIEVES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: grieve honestly, without a story on top. Sit, and let the breath settle. Let one loss come to mind, large or small, recent or old. Don't explain it. Don't look for a sign in it. If tears come, let them; in the report, they were called mercy. Just say to yourself what is true: this hurt, and I miss them. If you pray, you can say the line from the Qur'an that Muslims say at a loss: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning." If not, just stay with the plain sorrow, and breathe. The bell holds the time.
Maria and the eclipse. Maria the Copt, mother of Ibrahim, and the day the sun went dark and the Prophet said it was not for his son. Today's word.
Your line: the eyes weep, the heart grieves. Today, when something sad comes up, name it plainly to one person, without dressing it up or explaining it away. Day eight hundred seventeen.

howItsDone: When a solar or lunar eclipse happens, Muslims gather for salat al-kusuf, the eclipse prayer, with long recitation and bowing; at a death, Muslims often say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, we belong to God and to Him we return.

fork.setup: your son has just died, and the sun goes dark. people say the sky is mourning him. what do you say?
options: nothing: let the kind story comfort everyone.
agree: it's a sign of how loved he was.
correct them: the sun isn't eclipsed for anyone's death.
fork.reveal: in Bukhari he corrects them on the day of his grief, and tells them to pray until the eclipse clears.

original.note: Arabic: the eclipse of the sun; the prayer kept at an eclipse is salat al-kusuf.

trapdoor: what you thought: a sad story about a baby who died.
what it means: a father weeps openly, calls his tears mercy, and refuses to let people turn the eclipse into a sign about his son.
what a scholar hears: two separate reports in Bukhari, Anas on the tears and al-Mughirah on the eclipse, and the root of the eclipse prayer, salat al-kusuf.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1303 (Anas: the eyes weep, the heart grieves)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1043 (al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah: the eclipse on the day Ibrahim died)

notes: Bukhari 1303 and 1043 numbering and paraphrases: confirm (the tears report from Anas; the eclipse report from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah).
Maria's origin (sent from Egypt by its ruler) attributed to tradition in Ibn Sa'd; confirm.
Maria's standing (wife vs. umm walad) described as a difference among scholars without ranking; confirm the phrasing is fair.
Day 817 closes the part 'The mothers of the believers' (807–817); the teach says so in one line.
Ibrahim's age at death left out under the claims rule.
Editor: hook no longer says 'what many are thinking' (the report says people said it); 'Scholars differ' recast as 'some count her... others' under the claims rule; practice opener varied.
Audit: 'in the middle of the day' / 'AT MIDDAY' cut; the reports give no hour, and astronomical reconstructions of the eclipse at Medina place it in the morning.
